items.heading: A Research Scientist Is Not
items.text: A research scientist is not one job. It is a work mode, original investigation, experimental or theoretical rigour, and published or filed output, that exists inside at least four very different employers: a government lab, a corporate R&D division, an independent consulting practice, and a university.

items.heading: The Order Below Follows Real
items.text: The order below follows real growth and growth headroom as you gain reputation and proof, not which title sounds most respectable at a family gathering. Tracks with real ownership or an uncapped pay structure come first; tracks locked to a fixed government or UGC scale come later, regardless of how prestigious they sound.

rows: Roughly Rs 8-18 LPA at entry for an MSc/PhD, Rs 20-45+ LPA at senior scientist or principal-scientist level

Tech-sector research-scientist roles (AI/ML, semiconductors) at the top end of this range can run considerably higher for a strong PhD with a publication record. Pharma and FMCG R&D pay is typically steadier but with a lower ceiling than tech.
Highly variable, upside-driven; day rates or retainers rather than a fixed band

Patent/IP consultants, regulatory-affairs advisors, and technical due-diligence experts with 10+ years of real domain reputation can out-earn senior corporate scientists; someone with no visible track record earns very little at first.
Basic pay from roughly Rs 56,100/month (Level 10) at entry, rising through Scientist grades over 15-25+ years toward Level 14-15 for the small number of Outstanding Scientist

Same 7th Central Pay Commission matrix that applies to every central government post. A brilliant record does not move you outside this scale, only time-in-grade and a limited number of senior sanctioned posts do.
UGC/state scale from Level 10 basic ~Rs 57,700/month once confirmed; ad-hoc pay considerably lower
Covered in full detail, including the assistant-professor hiring pipeline, in the subject-specific PhD-outcomes guides linked below.
